page: Vultr vbm-8c-132gb is a dedicated bare metal server belonging to the Bare Metal NVMe family. It features an Intel Xeon 2288G processor built on the x86_64 architecture, offering 8 physical cores and 16 vCPUs running at a base clock speed of 3.7 GHz. The system is equipped with 128.0 GB of DDR4 memory operating at 3 GHz, providing 8.0 GB of RAM per core. Storage is bundled directly with the server, consisting of a 3840 GB local NVMe SSD. No GPU is included in this configuration.

Benchmark data indicates balanced performance across various workloads. The server demonstrates strong single-threaded performance in gzip compression (36.22 GB/sec) and bzip3 decompression (14.23 GB/sec). Its Passmark memory score is in the top tier, although large-block uncached memory bandwidth is relatively weak, with read speeds of 29.76 GB/sec and write speeds of 15.32 GB/sec. CPU benchmarks, including stress-ng and Geekbench, place both single-core and multi-core performance in the average range. Redis SET operations perform at an average rate of 17.28 million operations per second, and static web serving throughput reaches 11.49 GB/sec.

This bare metal configuration offers high resource density and dedicated hardware allocation, eliminating virtualization overhead. The combination of a high-capacity 3840 GB NVMe SSD and 128.0 GB of RAM makes it a cost-efficient choice for workloads requiring sustained, non-shared hardware access without the premium of GPU acceleration. It is appropriate for database hosting, software compilation, static web serving, and general-purpose bare metal applications. However, it is less optimal for memory-bandwidth-intensive tasks or large-scale LLM inference due to the weak performance observed in large-block memory transfers and 7B model processing.
